task.description: REQ-ANALYST drafted REQ-001 (i18n infrastructure, owner FRONTEND-DEV) and REQ-002 (Uzbek translations, owner CONTENT-BA, depends_on REQ-001) into docs/agents/requirements.yaml, in response to GitHub issue #2. Run WF-01 Step 2's full gate against both: TESTABILITY, CONSISTENCY, DEPENDS_ON CORRECTNESS, DESIGN-SYSTEM FIT, SIZE. Read both entries directly from docs/agents/requirements.yaml (grep -A 40 "id: REQ-001" / REQ-002) rather than trusting this summary. Pay particular attention to: (a) whether REQ-001's scope (routing restructure + library add + switcher UI) is genuinely one agent turn or should be split further, (b) whether the next-intl library choice and app/[locale] restructuring is consistent with this being a Next.js 16 App Router project with no prior i18n decision record to conflict with, (c) whether REQ-002's acceptance criteria are mechanically checkable by a script/diff as claimed, not just plausible-sounding, (d) whether the domain-vocabulary decision in REQ-002 is a legitimate call for REQ-ANALYST to make here or should have been escalated as a decisions/ draft instead (note: core-directives.md's Zero Manual Work item 1 requires escalating only when there are 'two or more genuinely equivalent options requiring a preference no agent can infer' — assess whether that threshold was actually met or whether REQ-ANALYST correctly inferred the answer from the existing Russian-verbatim precedent in content_ba_guide.md §4).
acceptance_criteria: Checks a-e from WF-01_requirement_development.md Step 2 are each explicitly run and recorded against both REQ-001 and REQ-002
Any FAIL cites the specific requirement id and check letter, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's validator-fail example shape
If PASS, result.summary states what was independently re-derived (which file was opened, which specific criteria were checked against which text), not just 'looks good'

result.summary: Read docs/agents/requirements.yaml directly (both full entries, lines 22-128) rather than trusting REQ-ANALYST's handoff summary, plus docs/agents/decisions/0001-full-pipeline-adopted.md (only decision on record, unrelated to i18n), docs/Design system for AI agents/readme.md in full, docs/guides/content_ba_guide.md, docs/guides/frontend_developer_guide.md, node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/internationalization.md (the doc REQ-001 cites), src/components/landing/Nav.tsx, src/app/globals.css, next.config.ts, and the actual project tree (no middleware.ts/proxy.ts, no tokens/ directory outside the docs folder). Checks (a) TESTABILITY, (b) CONSISTENCY, and (c) DEPENDS_ON pass for both requirements: all 9 acceptance criteria across REQ-001/REQ-002 are script/diff/grep/click-through checkable with no vague wording, no conflict with any done requirement or decision record exists, and REQ-002's depends_on:[REQ-001] is correct and complete. The domain-vocabulary decision in REQ-002 was a legitimate unilateral call, not an escalation case: content_ba_guide.md SS4 and the design system readme's 'Domain vocabulary (use verbatim)' list already state the verbatim-English rule with no locale carve-out, and the existing Russian copy already applies it (Nav.tsx's Russian labels translate ordinary nav words, never the domain tokens) -- extending a precedented rule to a new locale is inference from an existing record, not a choice between genuinely equivalent options core-directives.md SS1 would require filing as a decisions/ draft. Two checks FAIL, both on REQ-001. (d) DESIGN-SYSTEM FIT FAILS: REQ-001's scope-of-work text and AC5 both assert the Nav.tsx switcher must reuse classes 'already defined in tokens/components.css', but no such path exists in the project -- the only components.css is docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/components.css, a documentation-only reference file, and grepping it for '.lang'/'.nav' returns zero matches (the documented OKLCH design system does not define a nav or lang-switcher pattern at all). The actual .nav/.nav-in/.lang classes Nav.tsx uses live in src/app/globals.css (lines 35-51), built on this project's own bespoke variable set (--bg/--fg/--primary literals) that predates and diverges from the design system's documented tokens (--background/--foreground/--primary OKLCH values) -- similar names, not the same tokens. AC5 as written cannot be verified against the file it cites. (e) SIZE FAILS: REQ-001 bundles four materially distinct sub-tasks into one agent turn -- (1) adding next-intl as a dependency and committing to that library choice, (2) restructuring all of src/app/ under src/app/[locale]/ with new middleware/proxy (no middleware.ts or proxy.ts exists in the project today), (3) extracting hardcoded copy from 13 source files (layout.tsx plus the 12 landing components confirmed present: Band, Creed, Doors, Events, Footer, Hero, MapSection, Metrics, Nav, Partners, Streams, Team) into two new JSON message catalogs, and (4) building a working two-option locale switcher with routing-aware links, replacing Nav.tsx's confirmed-nonfunctional RU/UZ/EN spans. Per WF-01 Step 1c and core-directives.md's Weak-model tolerance principle, this asks one turn to introduce a new architectural layer, touch 13+ files, and land working UI interaction with no intermediate validation checkpoint -- it should be split, e.g. REQ-001a (next-intl + [locale] routing skeleton + switcher, catalogs seeded from layout.tsx only) depends_on-chained to REQ-001b (extract remaining 12 components' copy into the catalogs). Additionally noting as a MINOR (non-blocking) accuracy issue under check (b): REQ-001's rationale claims the Next.js doc's Resources section shows next-intl is 'the most actively maintained App-Router-native i18n library as of this writing' -- the actual doc (read in full) only lists next-intl first in an unordered, uncommented library list with no maintenance ranking language; the claim is REQ-ANALYST's own unstated inference presented as if sourced from the doc. This does not itself invalidate the library choice but should not be phrased as a doc citation.

issues.description: REQ-001 check (d) DESIGN-SYSTEM FIT: scope-of-work text and AC5 assert the Nav.tsx locale switcher must reuse classes 'already defined in tokens/components.css', but that path does not exist in the project (only docs/Design system for AI agents/tokens/components.css does, a reference-only doc file that itself contains zero .nav/.lang selectors). The .nav/.lang classes actually in use live in src/app/globals.css on the project's own bespoke variable set, not the documented design-system tokens. Rework must either point AC5 at the real file (src/app/globals.css) or explicitly decide/state whether the switcher should be migrated onto the documented OKLCH tokens instead -- not cite a nonexistent path.

REQ-001 check (e) SIZE: bundles (1) next-intl dependency/library decision, (2) src/app -> src/app/[locale] routing + middleware restructure, (3) copy extraction from 13 files into new message catalogs, and (4) a working locale-switcher UI into a single agent turn. Per WF-01 Step 1c, split into depends_on-chained requirements, e.g. routing/library/switcher skeleton first (catalogs seeded minimally) then full copy extraction second.

REQ-001's rationale attributes to node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/internationalization.md's Resources section the claim that next-intl is 'the most actively maintained App-Router-native i18n library as of this writing' -- the doc only lists it first among nine unranked, uncommented libraries. Rework should rephrase this as REQ-ANALYST's own assessment, not a doc citation.

result.next_action: Rework REQ-ANALYST -- rework iteration 1 of 3: (1) fix AC5/scope-of-work's tokens/components.css citation to reference the real file (src/app/globals.css) or explicitly address the divergence from the documented design-system tokens, (2) split REQ-001 into depends_on-chained requirements separating the i18n routing/library/switcher skeleton from the full 12-component copy extraction, (3) rephrase the next-intl rationale to not overstate what the Next.js doc's Resources section says. REQ-002 passed all five checks as drafted and needs no rework, but is blocked from WF-02 pending REQ-001's rework since its depends_on target is being reworked.
